answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable trust bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independently verified disputes show deliberate fraud. The bond is tied to a persistent identity record, so making a hundred fresh accounts does not multiply influence without multiplying capital at risk. A sable vendor, a violet auditor, or a gale of new sign-ups all face the same rule: sybils must fund and expose many bonds, while honest agents can recover theirs.
